finding_groups.suggestion: The skill description uses a broad catch-all trigger condition: “等类似表达时触发” (“or similar expressions”). This is not merely stylistic ambiguity in a prompt; for an agent skill, trigger conditions control routing and can affect which instructions get loaded into the model context. A loosely related user request may unintentionally activate this skill, especially if the routing system lacks a stricter intent classifier or explicit exclusion logic. The skill also instructs the agent to create/update files such as `docs/requirements/<功能名>.md` and `.progress/<功能名>.md`, so unintended activation can cause unwanted document creation or pollution of project state. In an adversarial context, an attacker could craft a superficially requirements-adjacent message to force this skill into play, potentially causing prompt-routing interference, excessive token consumption, creation of misleading requirement artifacts, or downstream confusion if those artifacts are later used by developers or modeling systems. This is a real operational/security weakness, though it is low-to-medium severity because the skill itself is benign, does not execute code, and mainly affects requirement documentation behavior. Replace vague activation language with precise, closed trigger conditions. For example, require explicit phrases such as “帮我写需求文档”, “把这份需求初稿整理成标准需求文档”, or “从原型反推需求”, and add negative examples such as “不要用于普通问答”“不要用于代码修改”“不要用于发布部署”. Add explicit exclusion conditions: the skill should not activate for general conversation, code review, bug fixing, model training, file deletion, secrets handling, or any request that does not explicitly ask for requirement documentation. Additionally, require user confirmation before writing files, confine all writes to an explicitly configured project directory, and prefer a stricter router/classifier over fuzzy semantic matching for activation.

results.description: LLM-as-Judge qualitative evaluation across 9 criteria (description clarity, instruction quality, trigger simulation, etc.)

findings.message: [9/10] Description is clear, specific, and explains WHEN to use the skill
findings.suggestion: The description clearly lists trigger phrases and states the skill’s purpose. It also explicitly excludes modeling, coding, and publishing.

findings.message: [9/10] Instructions are easy to follow with clear action steps
findings.suggestion: The workflow is divided into concrete phases, dimensions, progress files, and finalization steps. It is dense but very actionable.

findings.message: [7/10] Examples are helpful, relevant, show proper usage, AND cover sufficient query variations for robust skill detection
findings.suggestion: It provides many plain-language interview examples and several trigger phrases. It lacks explicit negative or edge-case queries for robust routing.

findings.message: [8/10] All necessary information is present (purpose, scripts, parameters)
findings.suggestion: Purpose, linked documents, templates, file paths, and completion conditions are all present. Scripts are not needed for this guidance skill.

findings.message: [9/10] Skill scope is well-defined (clear boundaries, not too broad/narrow)
findings.suggestion: The scope is clearly limited to requirement clarification and document production. Module, prototype, and draft inputs are handled as bounded variants.

findings.message: [7/10] Documentation uses professional, consistent tone and formatting
findings.suggestion: Formatting is consistent and structured. The tone is intentionally colloquial and forceful, which is less formally professional but suitable for non-technical users.

findings.message: [8/10] Mentally test the skill description against 5 plausible user queries that SHOULD trigger it and 3 that should NOT. Does the description enable correct routing without false positives or false negatives?
findings.suggestion: Most requirement-document requests would route correctly, and the no-code/no-model boundary reduces false positives. Phrases like “develop a feature” could still overlap with implementation requests.

findings.message: [9/10] Do the instructions cover a complete end-to-end workflow? Identify any steps where the user or agent would need to figure out what to do next without guidance.
findings.suggestion: The skill covers intent clarification, structured interviews, conflict checking, progress persistence, finalization, and special input modes. It is nearly end-to-end for its scope.

findings.message: [9/10] Are the documented error scenarios realistic and actionable? Would the solutions actually help resolve the issues, or are they generic boilerplate?
findings.suggestion: It addresses real failure modes such as context loss, contradictions, prototype placeholders, and premature closure. The mitigations are concrete and operationally useful.
